symptom: A DataGrid 2 column (or text box / pluggable attribute) bound to `System.Session_User/Administration.Account/FullName` — a path that steps down to a specialization of the hop's destination — passed check and exec, then mxbuild failed CE1613 "The selected attribute 'System.Session_User/Administration.Account/FullName' no longer exists." Naming the end itself (`System.Session_User/System.User/Name`) failed the same way
cause: `resolveAssociationAttributePath` read every segment before the attribute as an association; an entity segment failed the lookup, ok=false, and every caller fell back to writing the whole `/`-path as one flat attribute name
insight: The brief leaned towards a check refusal, and the measurement reversed it: mxbuild 11.14.0 accepts an AttributeRef whose EntityRefStep has DestinationEntity = the specialization (0 errors), and Studio Pro stores exactly that downcast on data sources (#2055) — the reporter's DESCRIBE note says Studio Pro authored such a column. Refusing would have been a false refusal of a Studio Pro construct. The cheap way to settle 'is there a writable shape' was a throwaway patch to the resolver plus one `docker check`, not reading BSON. Measure the 'legal twin' before trusting it: `Assoc/System.User/Name` was assumed legal and failed CE1613 too — only `Assoc/Name` was. Data source paths (`resolveAssociationHops`) already accepted `Assoc/Module.Entity`; the attribute-path resolver was the duplicate that lagged. One resolver serves columns, input widgets and the pluggable engine, so one fix covered all three (A/B on 11.14.0: base 3x CE1613, fixed 0). Still open: an entity off the hop falls back flat (CE1613, check silent), and DESCRIBE prints `Session_User/FullName` without the step. Tests `cmd_pages_builder_specialization_step_2127_test.go`; bug-test `mdl-examples/bug-tests/2127-attribute-path-through-specialization.mdl`
